Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the InnoMed Devices Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you may press star then one on your telephone. Please note, this call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements, including expectations regarding our future performance, business outlook, and financial results. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Joining me on today's call are Alex Thompson, CEO; Lisa Chen, CFO; and Dr. Marcus Lee, Chief Technology Officer.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Thompson.

Alex Thompson:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. InnoMed Devices delivered solid results this quarter, driven by strong execution and continued demand for our innovative medical device solutions.

Today, I will cover four key aspects of our performance:
1. Procedure volume trends and market recovery commentary,
2. Hospital and ambulatory surgery center adoption rates,
3. Overall performance highlights and key achievements,
4. Revenue and margin guidance for the next quarter/year.

Lisa will then provide a more detailed review of our financials. After that, we'll open the call for your questions.

Now, let's get started with procedure volume trends and market recovery commentary.

Procedure volumes remain the foundation of our growth in the medical devices sector, closely tied to operating room utilization, hospital throughput, and the uptake of our advanced technologies. Globally, volumes across our primary franchises increased by 14% year-over-year in Q2, continuing a streak of five straight quarters of double-digit gains and picking up speed from the 11% seen in Q1. This beats out peers—for instance, Medtronic's 9% cardiovascular growth and Stryker's 12% orthopedics volumes—thanks to a solid macroeconomic rebound and our dominant market positions.

Diving into franchises, cardiovascular, which makes up 45% of revenue, led with 18% volume growth, propelled by steady needs in structural heart and coronary procedures. Transcatheter aortic valve replacement volumes rose 22%, as minimally invasive approaches increasingly replace open surgeries, especially with aging populations. Our latest Evolut FX+ platform, featuring its suprannular leaflet design and reduced pacemaker rates of 8.5% based on U.S. real-world TVT Registry data, boosted our U.S. market share to 32%, from 28% last year. Drug-eluting stent volumes climbed 15%, aided by the Xience line's strong safety record in complex percutaneous coronary interventions, despite ongoing pricing challenges from CMS new technology add-on payments for ultra-thin struts. In electrophysiology, ablation procedures advanced 12%, helped by our Affera mapping system's seamless integration with pulsed-field ablation, which is building momentum in paroxysmal atrial fibrillation treatments, showing zero esophageal injuries in the MANIFEST-PF study.

Orthopedics, representing 30% of our mix, posted 13% growth, bouncing back strongly from delayed electives during the pandemic. Total joint replacements reached new highs, with knees up 16% and hips up 14%, in line with national rates from the American College of Surgeons' NSQIP database. Our Mako robotic-arm system shone, driving 28% growth in robot-assisted cases, now at 45% of U.S. ortho placements—surpassing Zimmer Biomet's ROSA—due to haptic feedback algorithms that cut soft-tissue impingement by 15% in kinematic alignment processes. Spine volumes grew more steadily at 9%, moderated by shifts to ambulatory settings, but our Aeris interbody fusion devices gained 20% in outpatient use, thanks to their 3D-printed porous structure that improves bone integration.

MedSurg and neuromodulation franchises saw 10% overall volume increases. Hernia mesh repairs and endoscopy procedures tapped into backlog demand, while our Inceptiv closed-loop spinal cord stimulator fueled 25% growth in chronic pain management, taking share from Abbott's Proclaim with better MRI-conditional features.

By region, recovery patterns vary but are positive overall. The U.S., 55% of sales, expanded 16% year-over-year, exceeding the 12% industry average from Definitive Healthcare, as hospital OR use settled at 85-90% and elective schedules normalized after CMS reinstated pass-through payments for robotics. Europe, 25% of revenue, grew 9%, held back by reimbursement issues like Germany's DiGA framework and France's CNAM caps on TAVR at €28,000, but we're encouraged by completing EU MDR and our CE Mark for the next-gen Hugo RAS system, which positions us for UK NHS tenders. Asia-Pacific surged 24%, with China up 32% from National Reimbursement Drug List inclusions for DES and TAVR via our MicroPort partnership for local Evolut production. Japan added 15% through better JMDN coverage for robotic orthopedics, and emerging markets like India and Brazil grew 18% via distributor pushes in secondary cities.

This isn't merely cyclical—structural drivers are at play. Demographics, like a projected 20% U.S. increase in octogenarians by 2030 per CMS, boost TAVR and neuromodulation demand. Our €250 million AI investment for procedure planning, such as the Myval THV's predictive hemodynamics, lifts case efficiency by 20% and clinician buy-in. Payer shifts help too: U.S. Medicare's 2% ASP cuts sting, but private bundles for robotic ortho at $35,000-$40,000 per case protect margins.

We're capitalizing strategically, ramping R&D to $1.2 billion yearly, or 12% of sales, focusing on pulsed-field ablation in EP and bioresorbable coronary scaffolds aiming for FDA Breakthrough by year-end. M&A is selective—our $800 million acquisition of a European robotic endoscopy firm strengthens our 15% share in single-port procedures. Pricing dipped 1% globally, countered by 3% value-based procurement mix, delivering 300 basis points of core margin expansion to 28.5%.

Now, let's talk about hospital and ambulatory surgery center adoption rates.

Adoption in hospitals and ASCs is pivotal for our MedTech lineup, especially our PrecisionNav robotic navigation system and Ascend minimally invasive orthopedic implants, which align with value-based care and outpatient shifts.

Headline figures: In Q2, overall adoption—facilities with active PrecisionNav or Ascend in their mix—hit 68% in our core U.S. and EU5 market of about 4,200 hospitals and 7,500 ASCs, up 12% year-over-year. ASC penetration leaped 22% to 41% from 28% last year, while hospital adoption stayed strong at 82%, with 4% growth from replacements and expansions in high-volume cardiac and neuro sites.

Hospitals, 65% of our $1.2 billion segment revenue, averaged 72 procedures per system monthly, up 8%, thanks to PrecisionNav 3.0's AI software with real-time haptic feedback and AR overlays, akin to Intuitive Surgical's da Vinci but ortho-spine focused, improving OR efficiency 18%. Wins include expansions at HCA Healthcare and Tenet, where we're standard in 62% of Level 1 trauma centers.

ASCs are the growth engine: Industry volumes rose 15% per SG Analytics, doubling inpatient pace on CMS 2024 OPPS boosts of 6.2% for MS-DRG 515-517 bundles. Our ASC adoption reached 41%, adding 320 sites—a 35% installed base jump. ASPs for compact PrecisionNav units held at $185,000, 5% over plan, as ASCs favor our low-power (40% less draw) systems and single-use Ascend kits cutting sterilization 25% vs. Zimmer Biomet trays.

U.S. led with 72% of new adoptions, 51% ASC penetration in Sun Belt states like Florida and Texas (2.3 ASCs per 100K population per Definitive Healthcare). Our ASC Accelerator Program onboarded 150 sites YTD with training and revenue support, achieving 92% retention. Europe at 32% adoption, up 18% post-CE Mark, with 25% install growth in Germany's 1,200+ ASCs under GKV-Spitzenverband ambulatory ortho push. Asia-Pacific surprised: China doubled to 15% via Mindray partnership (120 Tier 2 sites), Japan at 22% in 4,800 ASCs with NHI parity for robotic hips.

Our push includes the Site Optimization Suite for 45-to-65 monthly procedures via predictive analytics, tackling 30% idle time per OR Manager surveys. We're running seven Level 1 RCTs, like ASC-NAV vs. Stryker Mako showing 22% better TKA revisions. The $250 million OrthoFlex acquisition adds bioresorbable fixation for 15% ASC ASP uplift in bundles.

For Q3, ASC adoption to 45%, full-year 28% channel growth vs. 9% MedTech average per Evaluate MedTech. Supply risks for PrecisionNav chips are low at <2% via TSMC dual-sourcing.

Moving on to overall performance highlights and key achievements, as well as revenue and margin guidance—Lisa, over to you for the financial deep dive.

Lisa Chen:
Thank you, Alex. As Alex outlined, we achieved strong results across operations and adoption, translating to impressive financials this quarter.

Starting with highlights: InnoMed Devices outperformed in a tough medical devices environment, handling supply chain issues in semiconductors and materials, logistics inflation, and Medicare Advantage reimbursement changes. Our diversified portfolio in cardiovascular, orthopedics, neuromodulation, and robotics & endoscopy powered through.

Worldwide Q2 revenue hit $1.28 billion, up 18% organically—beating our 12-15% guide and the 8-10% industry per Evaluate MedTech. Constant currency was 19%, from post-COVID procedural recovery and share in high-acuity cases. Year-to-date revenue at $3.95 billion tracks to full-year midpoint of $5.3 billion, or 16% organic growth.

Adjusted EBITDA was $385 million, 30.1% margin—up 220 basis points—via 4% ASP hikes, LEAN manufacturing leverage, and high-margin capital mix. Non-GAAP diluted EPS of $1.42 topped consensus by $0.08, up 22% year-over-year. Free cash flow of $285 million funded $150 million share repurchases and a dividend raise to $0.35 per share, our 12th straight increase.

By segment, cardiovascular (42% of revenue) jumped 25% organically to $538 million. TAVR volumes set records, with EvoFlow valve at 14% U.S. share from 11%, challenging Edwards' Sapien and Medtronic's CoreValve. Structural heart grew 32% post-FDA Breakthrough for HeliX mitral clip. Coronary stents held mid-teens share with 15% global procedural rise.

Orthopedics rose 13% to $325 million, double-digits in hips/knees from elective backlog. U.S. up 18% under CMS bundles; Mako system (1.2 million procedures) drove 45% capital growth. Japan gained post-PMDA for cementless Trinity hip, offsetting EU MDR softness.

Neuromodulation/pain up 21% to $210 million; ReviX SCS at 27% U.S. penetration in refractory pain via AI closed-loop feedback, ahead of Abbott Proclaim and Boston Scientific WaveWriter.

Robotics & endoscopy soared 38% to $187 million; InnoBot Xi installed 165 units quarterly high, 92% utilization. Single-port endoscopy CE Mark in Europe eyes $200 million FY2025 revenue from outpatient shift.

Regions: U.S. (58%) up 22% on 9 million electives per Definitive Healthcare and InnoMed Academy training. Europe 12% despite procedural dips, via Galway manufacturing cutting duties 15%. APAC 25%, China 35% post-NMPA, India tapping $2.5 billion ortho via Stryker-like JV. Emerging markets now 8% of revenue from 6%.

Notable wins: FDA PMA for AI CardioVision imaging.

Turning to guidance for Q3 and FY2024. Q3 revenue $1.45-$1.48 billion, 8-10% reported or 9-11% organic growth, raised from $1.42-$1.46 billion on U.S. volumes and APAC. FX drag ~1 point from strong USD.

Segments: Cardiovascular (45%) 12% organic, mid-teens U.S. TAVR on CMS low-risk expansion like Boston Scientific's Lotus Edge; EMEA high-single. Ortho/spine 6-8%, Mako 25% installs offsetting trauma. Neuromodulation 15%+ on Inceptiv SCS (3% Q2 share vs. Medtronic Intellis).

Regions: U.S. (65%) 10-12% on 95% pre-COVID electives, ASCs to 28%. EMEA mid-single with TriClip TR adoption offsetting German DRGs. APAC high-teens, China 20%+ on NMPA Hugo RAS ahead of J&J Ottava; tariffs ~50bps COGS.

Q3 adjusted gross margin 67.5-68.0%, +150bps on Galway efficiencies (85% utilization), 72% CV disposables mix absorbing 100bps resin/nitinol inflation via 80% hedging.

Adjusted op margin 24.5-25.0%, +200bps; OpEx 43% with $50 million supply chain savings, Vietnam dual-sourcing post-USMCA.

FY2024 raised to $5.85-$5.95 billion, 7-9% reported/8-10% organic, Q4 low-double-digit. Gross margin 67.0-67.5% (+ from 66.5%) on $120 million productivity, automation, freight stabilization. Op margin 24.0-24.5%; EPS $4.85-$4.95, +10% midpoint with $500 million buyback.

This embeds 15-20% CAGR in robotics/structural to 2027 vs. 5-7% market. Initiatives: $450 million R&D (8% sales), 40% to AI imaging like Siemens AI-Rad cutting times 20%; JIT inventory frees $200 million capital; $300 million NeuroPace RNS for epilepsy. Risks: Medicare cuts (-1%), China delays (pivot Japan/India), FX.

Now, I'll turn the call back to Alex for Q&A.

Alex Thompson:
Thank you, Lisa. Operator, we are now ready to take questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for asking questions remain the same. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Alex, on procedure volumes, can you elaborate more on the bifurcation in Europe versus APAC and how China NRDL inclusions are influencing TAVR specifically?

Alex Thompson:
Great question, John. Europe's 9% growth reflects reimbursement hurdles like Germany's DiGA and France's €28,000 TAVR caps, but EU MDR completion and Hugo RAS CE Mark set us up for NHS wins. APAC's 24% is explosive, with China's 32% from NRDL adding our DES and TAVR—our MicroPort-localized Evolut production has accelerated that, capturing structural share as demographics drive octogenarian procedures up 20% by 2030 per CMS analogs. We're guiding Q3 volumes at 13-15%, full-year 12-14%, with 65% recurring from 12,000+ robotics base buffering risks like election volatility.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Maria Lopez with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Maria Lopez:
Lisa, helpful guidance raise. On margins, how are you thinking about the gross margin expansion sustainability given inflation and FX, and details on the productivity gains?

Lisa Chen:
Thanks, Maria. Q3 gross at 67.5-68.0% factors manufacturing ramps at Galway to 85%, high-margin disposables at 72% in CV, and hedging 80% of resin/nitinol exposure to offset 100bps inflation—similar to how we've managed Red Sea freight. FY gross to 67.0-67.5% includes $120 million from neuromod neuromodulation automation and freight normalization. OpEx discipline via $50 million savings and Vietnam sourcing keeps op margin expanding 200bps. Pricing flat at -1% but VBP mix adds 300bps core to 28.5% this quarter.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Kim with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

David Kim:
Thanks. Dr. Lee, on the adoption side, with ASCs at 41%, what's the tech edge in PrecisionNav versus Mako or ROSA, and pipeline for AI enhancements?

Dr. Marcus Lee:
Excellent point, David. PrecisionNav's haptic and AR overlays boost efficiency 18%, tailored for ortho/spine unlike da Vinci's general use, reducing impingement 15% in alignments. Site Optimization Suite uses predictive analytics to hit 65 procedures/month from 45, fixing idle time. RCTs like ASC-NAV show 22% better TKA outcomes vs. Mako. Upcoming: AI procedure planning from our €250 million investment, like Myval hemodynamics cutting times 20%, and $450 million R&D with 40% to imaging akin to Siemens, plus bioresorbables for scaffolds targeting Breakthrough.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Rachel Patel with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Rachel Patel:
Congrats team. On guidance risks, particularly China trade and Medicare—how much buffer, and M&A pipeline post-OrthoFlex/NeuroPace?

Alex Thompson:
Thanks, Rachel. China tariffs modeled at 50bps COGS, but NMPA for Hugo positions us ahead; contingency is Japan/India ramps. Medicare sequestration at -1% revenue hit, offset by private bundles at $35k-40k robotic ortho. M&A opportunistic like $800 million endoscopy tuck-in for single-port 15% share, $250 million OrthoFlex for ASC uplift, $300 million NeuroPace for epilepsy—aiming high-margin robotics CAGR 15-20% to 2027.

Alex Thompson:
Thank you for your questions. Before we conclude, I want to reiterate our confidence in the long-term growth potential of InnoMed Devices. We are committed to delivering innovative medical device solutions that improve patient outcomes and create value for our shareholders.

Thank you for joining us today.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
